Going after Gupta's

By: Joy Summers | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
After months of inaction finally the Asset forfeiture unit is going after funds in Gupta linked companies

Unique Selling Point:
Today the NPA has confirmed that they are serving a preservation order to freeze R1.6 billion rand of assetts linked to international consulting company Mckinsey and the Gupta linked Trilliian. Is it too late or will justice finally be done. Carte Blanche covers this developing story.

Summary:
On Monday evening the City Press dropped a bombshell. After months of no action the Asset forfeiture unit had been sitting on an ex parte order to freeze R1.6 billion rand of Trillian and Mckinsey that Eskom itself admitted they should not have paid. Later on Monday evening more information confirmed by the NPA that mining minister Mosebenzi Zwane could face arrest for his role in the Estina dairy matter.

Behind the scenes the new trade union federation SAFTU under the leadership of Zwelenzima Vavi has been working with the NPA as well as other NGO’S like OUTA. In October they laid charges and have been collating information to get to this point.

At Eskom Suzanne Daniels – suspended head of legal told the Eskom parliamentary inquiry that she wrote the report to Minister Lynne Brown recommending that Trillian and Mckinsey pay back the money to Eskom. A few days later she was suspended.

Carte Blanche speaks to Suzanne Daniels about her experience as a whistleblower and how she feels now that a state institution is going after the money. We also chat to Zwelenzima Vavi, OUTA and the NPA and follow this developing story

Press Release:



First Strike From The AFU
This week the Asset Forfeiture Unit launched their first strike against international consulting company McKinsey and the Gupta-linked company, Trillian. Their preservation order freezes R1.6 billion, but that is just the beginning, says the NPA. They hope to recover another R50- billion. In an exclusive interview, Carte Blanche sits down with Suzanne Daniels, the Eskom executive, who was the first to recommend these companies pay back the money, but was suspended shortly afterwards.


Script:


FINAL SCRIPT AFU

Commentary One
On Monday Afternoon journalist Abram Mashego broke another big story. The NPA's Asset forfeiture unit had been granted an order to freeze the assets of American consulting company McKinsey and the Gupta linked company Trillian.

LINK
As the depth of state capture became clear, Civil society, unions pushed back, each playing a part, but it was SAFTU which laid the charges against Trillian and McKinsey

Commentary Two
Zwelinzima Vavi is the General Secretary of new union SAFTU

Vavi
We are hitting them now where it hurts the most, their pockets and with that you will begin to see the ground shifting

Commentary Three
But the ground may not have shifted without the testimonies of three women who blew the whistle on billions of rands paid to McKinsey and Trillian by Eskom in what the Asset forfeiture unit is now describing as theft, fraud, money laundering and corruption.

Devi
What role have whistleblowers played?
Vavi
Unbelievable! The two women whose names must be written in diamonds in the history books inside Trillian who saw the money moving and started to blow the whistle and those women must be kept safe
Devi
The real hero's
Vavi
The real hero's! Without these people we would whisper around dinner tables with no evidence

Commentary four
Mosilo Mothepu and Belinda Goodson, both former CEO's of Trillian companies, took on the powerful Gupta network that reached right up to the President, and from inside Eskom, Suzanne Daniels did the same.

Devi
Why did you go after for Trillian?
Vavi
There is Salim Essa there he is the kingpin in the whole network Gupta capturers



Commentary Five
Until now neither of the former Trillian company women have appeared on television. On Friday evening Bianca Goodson told us her story

Bianca
Shortly after I signed my employment contract …..the first excel spreadsheets were shared with me from McKinsey and that indicated R 10 billion rand over 3 years. I fell over in my chair. That was one of these big red flags, because in my mind no one gets that lucky

Commentary six
That is the amount Eskom was going to pay McKinsey for their at- risk contract. Trillian, owned then by Salim Essa, sometimes referred to as the 4th Gupta brother, would be McKinsey's BEE partner, and for that McKinsey and Trillian would offer advice on how to save Eskom money. It was this deal that piqued the interest of investigative journalist Susan Comrie

Susan
Consulting fees in a way, they are such a perfect way to leach money out of the state.

Commentary seven
For months last year she combed through documents to understand how Eskom was ripped off

Susan
In Mckinsey's case the contract is so abusive, it's so clearly designed in Mckinsey's favour to rip money out of Eskom - this is a company that says they will act in the best interests of the client and not in the best interests of the firm Mckinsey and in this case look at that contract and think that they have lived up to that in any instance in that contract

Commentary eight
When we asked McKinsey for an interview they sent a press statement instead. In it McKinsey say that they stand by their statement of 17th October 2017 in which they categorically rejected the notion that their firm was involved in any acts of bribery or corruption related to their work at Eskom.

Devi
What was their actual job
Susan
So McKinsey and Trillian, their job was to come in and find savings for Eskom
Devi
That sounds like a great idea
Susan
… good idea in theory because if you don't make any savings for Eskom you won't get paid, the problem was that McKinsey and Trillian ended up getting paid, simply for coming up with ideas …if you implement this project we estimate that this is the savings that you will make - what Eskom did is sign off and say great we will give you 10% of those theoretical savings

Commentary nine
But only months into the contract, McKinsey ended their relationship with Trillian and the whole thing came to a sudden end. But McKinsey and Trillian still sent letters of demand to Eskom for the balance, and that is where Suzanne Daniels comes in.

Suzanne Daniels
By the time we were asked to look at the documents R937 million had already been paid

Commentary ten
In November Suzanne Daniels used parliaments protective disclosure at the Eskom Inquiry to blow the whistle on Megawatt Park's secrets

Up sound
There is only one way to describe this was brazen theft

Link
Suzanne Daniels had risen up the ranks at Eskom, but her career came to an abrupt halt after she recommended that McKinsey and Trillian pay back the money

Susan Comrie
The Eskom executives involved in this were quite keen after the project came to an end, to just settle as fast as possible, Anoj Singh and the other executives said to the Eskom board lets pay them R1.8 billion and be done with this. Those executives were trying to close the book on this as fast as possible, what happens is that Suzanne Daniels comes along and she reopens it and that is how we know about all these things that have happened

Commentary eleven
By Feb 2017 Daniels finally had a complete picture of the deal. We now know that Trillian had no contract with Eskom, but was paid almost R600 million rand by the utility

Suzanne
The contracts were manufactured. Contract numbers were made to suit the payment, Purchase order numbers were created at the time of invoicing and linked to what we now know as fictitious contracts because those contracts didn't exist. There is no documentation
Devi
No contracts but invoices and payments?
Suzanne
Invoices and payments yes
Devi
No contract but R937 million paid but M and Trillian were asking for the balance
Yes
Bit of a cheek isn't it if there wasn't even a contract
Suzanne
Yes, that is why we asked for the money back because it was irregular in terms of the PFMA


Commentary twelve
Daniels recommended to the board that Eskom should lay criminal charges, but her team was beginning to step on toes

Devi: When did you get to the point when you thought that is it, I have a story to tell
Suzanne
I had already reached that point between July and September. We were frustrated. there were internal threats to my team, they were intimidated, refused information. They were extremely rattled. I am surprised they are still standing, they really had to fear for their safety.

Commentary thirteen
Information on this dodgy deal was also starting to leak beyond Megawatt Park - Lynne Brown was asked in parliament if Trillian had been paid by Eskom. Under oath she said no

Devi
Did Eskom try to cover this up?
Susan
Undoubtedly! When we first did stories in May last year to say here is the evidence that Trillian got paid Eskom still denied it

Commentary fourteen
It took almost a year before Eskom's chairman of the board was forced to admit the payments at the July results last year. Eskom have declined our request for an interview and Trillian have not replied

Zethemba Khoza at Eskom
Trillian was subcontracted to McKinsey when Eskom was requested to pay them directly R495 million and MCKENZIE R900 million total R1. 4 billion

Commentary fifteen
After marching and tweeting against state capture, by October, Vavi decided it was time to go after the money.

Zwelenzima Vavi
We had sent an affidavit to the Hawks the NPA and said here is your evidence we want you to act - Sean Abrahams said we are investigating but will only act on police investigation - arrogantly saying to us go and sit down

Commentary sixteen
But Vavi is not the kind of man to go and sit in a corner

Zwelenzima Vavi
We said you have 14 days to act here is your evidence and we were told they went into a panic because any court seeing that affidavit with its overwhelming evidence would have said you are refusing to carry forward their oath of office

Commentary seventeen
Many South Africans have lost faith in the NPA under Sean Abrahams. Corruption watch say his loyalty lies not with the law but with President Jacob Zuma and his cronies. NPA spokesman Luvuyo Mfaku rejects that claim

Luvuyo
Look the assertion by Corruption watch is really unfair and unfounded. Remember the AFU derives its power from the National director.
Devi
That is Sean Abrahams
Luvoyo
That is Sean Abrahams yes. If he wanted to stall he would not have given them the authority
In fact, Sean Abrahams has given them stringent time lines saying guys you need to finalise these things you can't investigate in perpetuity

Commentary eighteen
By Tuesday the NPA confirmed that more was coming.
Devi
So, the NPA has said they are going after assets of R50 billion
Vavi Claps

Commentary nineteen
For Daniels, Mothepu and Goodson, the NPA's action vindicates their claims. But their disclosures have taken their toll.

Bianca Goodson
It's been the weirdest journey that nobody, nobody can empathise with. Where you can't …and you get support from strangers and you are lonely and you are scared and you don't know what tomorrow is going to look like and all in between of that life goes on right -
For me I have been lucky it's been a year, it's been longer for Mosilo, it's been worse for her and Suzanne is still going through it, Suzanne Daniels.

Commentary Twenty
Daniels is still fighting to get her job back and she refutes the claims Eskom has made against her. Things went wrong in September when she wrote this report to Minister Lynne Brown and recommended to the board, McKinsey and Trillian pay back the money

Suzanne Daniels
And I saw this as an opportunity to give her all the information and I was hopeful she would do something with it
Devi
What happened after that?
Nothing, except that I get lambasted for glaring gaps in the report
Devi
By Whom

Suzanne
By the minister

Commentary twenty-one
In September, once the report was in - everything changed

Suzanne
From that moment on the board excluded me
Devi
On what basis
Suzanne
I don't know based on the ministers release, they tried to paint me as an executive gone rogue and I did this all on my own

Commentary Twenty- two
Daniels once admired executives like Matshela Koko and Anoj Singh. But in parliament she accused them of theft, a claim they have vigorously denied.

Suzanne
on a personal level that was quite devastating for me, these were people I respected and admired, Matshela was a good decision maker. I think Anoj was the first CFO in a while who had an understanding of what was happening. It was quite devastating to realize their positions they actually used it for other purposes

Commentary Twenty- three
This week ratings agency Standard and Poor's cautioned there was a real danger that Eskom could default on its loans, the finance minister said that Eskom keeps him awake at night, and senior executives petitioned Cyril Ramaphosa to urgently intervene. Then on Saturday Zethembe Khoza, chairman of the board resigned and a new board to strengthen governance at Eskom was finally announced.

Then on Saturday the chairman of the board resigned, a new board was announced, and it could be the end of the road for Matshela Koko and Anoj Singh


THE END 13 19

PROMO ONE
Whistleblowers speak out on Eskom's deal with McKinsey and Trillian
Suzanne
They tried to paint me as an executive gone rogue and I did this all on my own

PROMO TWO
This week the NPA confirmed they had frozen the assets of McKinsey and the Gupta linked Trillian and that was just the beginning
Devi
They say R50 billion
Vavi claps



PROMO THREE
The NPA are investigating Eskom's R1.6 billion payment to McKinsey and Trillian, but it was whistleblowers who laid the foundation for their investigation
Bianca
and you are lonely and you are scared and you don't know what tomorrow is going to look like

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): After months of inaction finally the Asset forfeiture unit is going after funds in Gupta linked companies
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Today the NPA has confirmed that they are serving a preservation order to freeze R1.6 billion rand of assetts linked to international consulting company Mckinsey and the Gupta linked Trilliian. Is it too late or will justice finally be done. Carte Blanche covers this developing story.
metadata.Summary: On Monday evening the City Press dropped a bombshell. After months of no action the Asset forfeiture unit had been sitting on an ex parte order to freeze R1.6 billion rand of Trillian and Mckinsey that Eskom itself admitted they should not have paid. Later on Monday evening more information confirmed by the NPA that mining minister Mosebenzi Zwane could face arrest for his role in the Estina dairy matter. Behind the scenes the new trade union federation SAFTU under the leadership of Zwelenzima Vavi has been working with the NPA as well as other NGO’S like OUTA. In October they laid charges and have been collating information to get to this point. At Eskom Suzanne Daniels – suspended head of legal told the Eskom parliamentary inquiry that she wrote the report to Minister Lynne Brown recommending that Trillian and Mckinsey pay back the money to Eskom. A few days later she was suspended. Carte Blanche speaks to Suzanne Daniels about her experience as a whistleblower and how she feels now that a state institution is going after the money. We also chat to Zwelenzima Vavi, OUTA and the NPA and follow this developing story
